articleTitle: OMN 2017 keynote speakers
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Provides an abstract for each of the keynote presentations and may include a brief professional biography of each

articleTitle: OMN 2017 invited speakers
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Provides an abstract for each of the presentations and may include a brief professional biography of each presenter. The complete presentations were not made available for publication as part of the conference proceedings.

articleTitle: An ultra-fast electrothermal micromirror with bimorph actuators made of copper/tungsten
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: This paper reports an ultra-fast electrothermal bimorph micromirror with an inverse-series-connected bimorph actuator, which is made up of Cu-W bimorph. This mirror has a high rotational resonant frequency of 12.8 kHz.

articleTitle: Frequency-mixing in GaAs dielectric metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate resonantly enhanced nonlinear optical processes such as 2nd-, 3rd-, and 4th-harmonic generations, sum-frequency generation, four-wave mixing processes, etc., in the visible and near-IR using GaAs dielectric metasurfaces.

articleTitle: MEMS 3-dimensional scanner for handheld confocal microscope
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: A MEMS scanning mirror based on a deformable SU-8 membrane mirror supported by a biaxial gimbal with SU-8 flexures delivers 3-dimensional beam scanning for a handheld confocal microscope. Beam scanning and focusing performance are characterized.

articleTitle: MEMS micromirror based light sheet generator for biomedical imaging
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Two MEMS micromirrors with resonant or static actuation are used as a MEMS enabled light sheet generator, with light sheet dimensions of 3.5 μm by 550 μm and offset positioning of 150 μm in the focal plane.

articleTitle: Mode-group mixing device via complex phase masks printed on fiber tip
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We introduce a novel, low loss and compact mode scrambler, printed directly on fiber-connector. The device is optimized to flatten inter-mode-group mixing level over all mode-groups at minimum loss for strong mixing in FMF links.

articleTitle: Fabrication of PbS quantum dots and silicon device for near-infrared detection
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Imaging devices for near-infrared wavelengths on silicon large scale integration (LSI) are very attractive for secure applications. We here demonstrate an LSI-compatible hybrid IR detector by integrating PbS quantum dots the surface of silicon.

articleTitle: Nanoscale silicon truncated conical photodetector at subwavelength aperture for NSOM applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Silicon-based photodetector sharing subwavelength aperture and shaped as a truncated conical-probe, has been electrically and optically simulated. Designed for NSOM, it may collect near-field surface information with clear advantage of a resolution inaccessible by conventional optical microscopy. Results present a promising device for several wavelengths.

articleTitle: A compact MEMS-based wide-angle optical scanner
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: A compact laser scanner that scans approximately 90° has been demonstrated, which is enabled by an electrothermal MEMS mirror encapsulated in a 3D printed holder with a curved dome for optical amplification.

articleTitle: Aperture arrays for subnanometer calibration of optical microscopes
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We fabricate and test subresolution aperture arrays as calibration devices for optical localization microscopy. An array pitch with a relative uncertainty of approximately three parts in ten thousand enables localization with subnanometer accuracy.

articleTitle: GaN microring waveguide bonded to Si substrate by polymer
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Hybrid integration of GaN and Si photonic devices is promising. Using a polymer bonding technique, GaN microring resonators are fabricated on Si substrate. Transmission characteristics of the GaN microring is measured.

articleTitle: Two-axis quasistatic gimbal-less microscanner with concentrically tilted stationary comb electrodes
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Two-axis quasistatic gimbal-less microscanners were fabricated through the microassembly of a glass lid and stationary comb electrodes. The total optical scan angles were enlarged to 5.2° and 5.8° for horizontal and vertical scan axes, respectively.

articleTitle: Tunable corner cube retroreflector (CCR) fabricated with 3D printing and origami
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: In this paper, we demonstrate a single-piece tunable corner cube retroreflector fabricated with 3D printing and origami. A process to fabricate optical components by 3D printing has also been developed.

articleTitle: Analog Silicon Photonic MEMS phase-shifter with double-step electrostatic actuation
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We present the design of an analog Silicon Photonic MEMS phase shifter based on vertically moving adiabatic couplers. Using a two-step electrostatic actuation method, the phase shifter can be turned on selectively by applying an actuation voltage on a first pair of electrodes, and the phase of the optical signal can be tuned continuously by applying an actuation voltage at a second electrode pair. A mechanical movement of only 20nm at 19V actuation voltage allows for a full π phase shift. The design exhibits a compact footprint of 60um × 44um and low excess insertion loss below 0.1dB.

articleTitle: Ultra-thin plasmonic metal nitrides: Tailoring optical properties to photonic applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: In this study, we present recent developments on growing epitaxial quality, ultra-thin titanium nitride films that exhibit very good metallic/plasmonic properties, comparable with their bulk counterparts. The potential of these films for extreme light confinement and electrical control is discussed.

articleTitle: A photonic MEMS accelerometer with a low-finesse hemispherical microcavity readout
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: This paper describes the design, fabrication, and testing of a photonic MEMS accelerometer that uses a hemispherical microcavity to transduce the motion of the proof mass. The cavity design provides stable operation that is relatively tolerant of misalignment errors. The prototype sensor is shown to have optical resonances that closely match the expected Airy function model.

articleTitle: Characterization and reliability study of a MEMS mirror based on electrothermal bimorph actuation
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: An electrothermal bimorph based MEMS mirror with large scan range, high fill factor and high resonant frequency is presented. A reliability issue due to burn-out of a bimorph thermal actuator is also studied and modeled.

articleTitle: Solid non-mechanical discretely-tunable hard-aperture diaphragm
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: In this paper, we demonstrate a solid non-mechanical discretely-tunable hard-aperture diaphragm. The device can switch between different aperture sizes (3 mm and 7 mm) by changing the applied voltage.

articleTitle: Selective in-plane Fabry-Pérot gas sensor functionalized with polymer
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Smell is one of the last senses still not completely replicated. Artificial gas sensors do manage to reach enough sensitivity but selectivity is still an issue. However, it is essential to several industries and smart cities. In this work, the selectivity of a previously reported optical gas sensor is demonstrated using three polymers for functionalization. Different sensitivities are obtained for toluene, 1-butanol, limonene and valeric acid.

articleTitle: Mouse tissue imaging using real-time Lissajous confocal endomicroscopic system
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We present mouse tissue imaging using real-time Lissajous confocal endomicroscopic system. The system consists of endomicroscopic catheter, confocal imaging system, and image processing module. The system obtained 2D fluorescence ex-vivo imaging results of mouse tissue.

articleTitle: CD-like centrifugal microfluidic device for organophosphorus pesticides (OPP) sensing
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: A centrifugal microfluidic device (CMD) is demonstrated for organophosphorus pesticides (OPP) sensing. CMD is designed as a CD-like to have a sequential sample injection with capillary valves controlled by centrifugal force, i.e. rotational speed (rpm). OPP in CMD could be successfully derived into a mixer at 570 rpm and then spined into a detection reservoir at 2000 rpm. The experiment results indicated that limit of detection (LD) for OPP is 0.01 ppm. A linear relationship between OPP logarithmic concentration (ppm) and inhibition rate is 0.9215.

articleTitle: Tunable terahertz bandpass filter using MEMS reconfigurable metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We report on a tunable terahertz bandpass filter based on a cross-shaped slot resonator with a reconfigurable roll-up micro structures. The built-in capacitors within the resonator are electrostatically actuated to shift the resonant frequency.

articleTitle: A refractive index sensor based on a packaged microfiber coil resonator
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We demonstrate a refractive index sensor based on microfiber coil resonator packaged with polydimethylsiloxane to detect glucose solutions with different concentrations. The detection limit of this sensor was about 7×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−4</sup>.

articleTitle: Cryogenic testing of MOEMS deformable mirror for future optical instrumentation
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: An Iris AO MOEMS deformable mirror has been successfully operated and tested at 160K. Surface deformation at room temperature and in cryo has been measured and DM architecture contributions analyzed.

articleTitle: Micromachined drilling of dielectric substrates of varying bandgap using laser accelerated particles
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: It has been observed that absorbing particles accelerated by Continuous Wave (CW) lasers initiate catastrophic failure in the form of micromachined drill holes. This process was tested using stainless steel, PMMA, and silica particles with fused silica, sapphire, and spinel substrates. Hole drilling occurred at laser power densities as low as 250kW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, far below the damage thresholds seen in typical situations. A potential dependence of accelerated particle breakdown on substrate bandgap may suggest that the underlying physical process is similar to that seen for CW laser breakdown of contaminated optical coatings.

articleTitle: Q-switched tunable solid-state laser using a MOEMS mirror
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Simultaneous wavelength tuning and Q-switching of a Yb:KGW laser using a single, electrothermally actuated MOEMS mirror is reported for the first time. A 15.4 nm tuning range is achieved at 2.06 kHz pulse repetition frequency.

articleTitle: Antireflective structures for tunable liquid-filled lens
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: This work presents novel antireflective structures (ARS) on flexible membrane for tunable liquid-filled lens by using wafer-level MEMS fabrication. ARS on flexible membrane with enhanced optical transmittance will provide new visions for miniaturized camera systems.

articleTitle: High-efficiency, low-aspect-ratio planar lens based on Huygens resonators
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Most designs of dielectric planar lenses mainly rely on the waveguide effect of high-aspect-ratio nanostructures. We demonstrate the design of high-efficiency, high-numerical-aperture, and low-aspect-ratio planar lenses for visible light, based on TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> Huygens resonators.

articleTitle: Flat and conformal optics with dielectric metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: I discuss our dielectric metasurface platform based on high index nano-posts on a low index substrate, and its applications in imaging, dispersion control, retroreflection and conformal optics.

articleTitle: Injection locking of optomechanical oscillators via acoustic waves
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We demonstrate injection locking of an optomechanical oscillator to an electromechanical oscillator through acoustic waves. The locking range is measured as a function of acoustic excitation strength for two different configurations.

articleTitle: Effectively anticancer drug concentration gradients by using 3D microfluidic chip
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: A 3D microfluidic chip for resistance of H460 lung cancer cells (LCC) was demonstrated. H460 LCC could be restrained by the injection of different curcumin concentration and investigated in different microenvironmental pH conditions. In the range of curcumin concentration of 57.2-100 μg/mL, the average apoptosis rate (AR) of H460 LCC were 53.6%, 58.4%, and 98.0% for pH=6.5, 7.4, and 8.5 microenvironments, respectively. The resistant efficiency of H460 LCC could be enhanced substantially at pH=8.5 microenvironmental condition. These results pave a way for using 3D microfluidic chip in cell biology application.

articleTitle: Optomechanical spring effect readout in resonant micro-optical Sagnac gyroscopes design and scaling analysis
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We propose and theoretically analyze a new cavity optomechanical oscillator gyroscope. Mechanical frequency acts as a sensitive readout of rotation through the optomechanical spring and Sagnac effects. Remarkably, reducing device size improves scale factor.

articleTitle: Enabling trapped ion quantum computing with MEMS technology
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Practical-scale quantum computing using trapped atomic ions requires non-conventional integration technologies in mechanical and optical domains. We present the design and operation of our system where MEMS technology provides critical enabling components.

articleTitle: Phase control through Huygens' metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We describe a dielectric Huygens' metasurface, operating in the visible spectrum, that can manipulate the phase of the transmitted light over a full 2π with high transmission efficiency. The metasurface is comprised of dielectric cylindrical nanoparticles embedded in a glass-like medium. The size of the nanoparticles and their separation are much smaller than the wavelength of visible light. From the metasurface, we construct a lens that focuses light to a diffraction limited spot size with high efficiency.

articleTitle: Endoscope zoom optics using Alvarez lenses
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We report an ultra-compact endoscopic optical zoom system having two tunable Alvarez lenses. The endoscope optics has a diameter about 2 mm and length of 20 mm, and is capable of continuously optical zooming close to 3× from field of view 50° to 18° with satisfactory imaging performances.

articleTitle: Dual-band tunable graphene-based filter
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We have demonstrated a scalable dual-band tunable infrared filter based on gating of a continuous graphene layer. The measured and modeled response of the device are in good agreement.

articleTitle: A new extremely small sensor for measuring a blood flow and a contact pressure simultaneously
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: A number of laser Doppler blood flow sensors have been developed over the past few decades. However, they remain uncommon in practice. This is because the contact pressure between the skin and the sensor is not measured simultaneously with blood flow, despite the fact that blood flow is greatly affected by contact pressure. Thus, reliable and highly reproducible measurement of blood flow could not be realized. Therefore, we have developed a micro electro mechanical systems (MEMS) blood flow sensor which has a built-in pressure sensor, for reliable and highly reproducible measurement.

articleTitle: Batch production of silicon fiber-top cantilever devices
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We present a fabrication procedure for batch production of MEMS devices directly on top of an optical fiber. Here, the stepwise fabrication procedure is described and the performance of the final device is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Two-axis MEMS scanner in a resonance operation for diagnosis of middle ear diseases
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: A two-axis electrostatic MEMS scanner was fabricated to realize an OCT probe for middle ear diagnosis. Scanning angles were up to 8 degrees at resonance and the temperature dependence was within 1.2%.

articleTitle: Development of selective pattering method of biomolecules using photothermal effect on engineering plastic micro wells
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Selective attachment of biomolecules to micro wells contributes to fabrication of biodevices and biosensors. The biomolecules can be patterned on the engineering plastic micro wells by using the photothermal method. Our method provides a highly selective and highly resolved patterning method.

articleTitle: Polarization insensitive metamaterial perfect absorber at visible frequencies
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: A novel metamaterial absorber with broadband and polarization-insensitive response is proposed. Simulation and experimental results indicates high absorption efficiency in the visible range. This metamaterial absorber offers potential application in development of photovoltaics and thermal detection.

articleTitle: Keynote Th-K: Integrated optomechanical and superconducting quantum circuits
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: I will present recent work at Caltech on the integration of optomechanical crystals for light and sound with electronic superconducting quantum circuits. Utilizing the silicon-on-insulator (SOI) wafer platform, we have made key advances in the fabrication and integration of extremely low loss microwave phonon structures and low loss microwave superconducting resonators of high impedance. These technical advancements offer several intriguing opportunities for quantum information processing and networking with phonons, photons, and electrons in an integrated, wafer-scale platform. The focus of my talk will be on two examples of our efforts in this direction: (i) nonreciprocal photon transport and amplification arising from synthetic magnetic flux and reservoir engineering in an optomechanical crystal circuit, and (ii) waveguide-QED systems consisting of microwave-bandgap circuits with embedded transmon-like qubits.

articleTitle: Fabrication of varifocal scanner integrated with piezoresistive focal length and angle sensor
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We present the varifocal scanner combined with the piezoresistors to monitor the rotation angle and focal length. The angle sensor measures with the accuracy of ±0.021 degree in the range of ±1.2 degree.

articleTitle: On-chip manipulation of local heating and nanoparticle motion
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We exploit the resonant enhancement of light in photonic crystal slabs to enhance selected optical properties. Enhancement of absorption and local field gradients result in applications to microscale heating and optical trapping, respectively.

articleTitle: Third order nonlinear waveguide with CdSe quantum dots in PFCB nanocomposite core
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We present our implementation of waveguides for third order nonlinear interactions constructed of 1.3% volume concentration CdSe quantum dots in PFCB polymer. FWM phenomena was observed and waveguide nonlinear coefficient of 7(Wm)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> was evaluated.

articleTitle: Integrated spectrometer and displacement sensor based on mechanically tunable photonic crystals
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We present a nano-opto-electro-mechanical sensor based on electrostatically tunable double-membrane photonic crystal cavities. We demonstrate free-space and waveguide coupling schemes for the input light, while the readout is provided by an integrated quantum dot photodiode.

articleTitle: A novel silicon microsphere based optical fiber probe for refractive index sensing applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: A new optical fiber probe based on in-line silicon microsphere cavity Fabry-Pérot interferometer (FPI) was demonstrated for refractive index sensing applications with a sensitivity about -5.326±0.223/RIU.

articleTitle: Broadband mid-infrared silicon-on-insulator waveguide devices
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We demonstrate SOI waveguide with low propagation and bending loss of 2dB/cm and 0.02dB/90° in the broad mid-infrared range of 3.68-3.88μm. By theoretically analyzing loss mechanisms, we indicate SOI waveguide's intrinsic limitation for mid-infrared application.

articleTitle: Keynote Mo-K: Graphene for next generation silicon photonics
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We show that graphene can be provide electro-optic properties to traditionally passive optical materials and enable efficient integrated active nanophotonic devices. We show devices with GHz absorption modulation based on ring resonators. We also report the first experimental demonstration of a graphene electro-refractive modulator with V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">π</inf>L of 0.14 V cm, and minimal absorption modulation based on graphene capacitor integrated on Si3N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> with embedded high-K and high breakdown dielectric.

articleTitle: Developing X-ray photonic microsystems for synchrotron applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We take this opportunity to introduce our research and development effort on MEMS-based dynamic x-ray optics that exploit the properties to manipulate and control the x-ray pulses at synchrotron sources for time-resolved experiments.

articleTitle: Sub-10-nanometer-scale laser ablation on hard materials from dielectric near-field nanophotonics
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: This paper demonstrates sub-10-nanometer (nm) laser ablation on hard materials. An 800-nm-wavelength femtosecond laser is focused down to sub-diffraction-limited scale by a silicon nanophotonic structure fabricated on a silicon-on-isolator (SOI) substrate, which is utilized to enable the ablation on the silicon dioxide (SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) layer of the SOI. Atomic force microscopy (AFM) results show a minimum ablation linewidth of about 8 nm with a depth-to-width ratio close to 1.

articleTitle: Active electromechanical resonance tuning of localized gap plasmons
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We present a nanoelectromechanical system with integrated localized gap plasmon resonators. The system enables broad tuning of plasmonic resonances and subdiffraction, high-sensitivity optical sensing of nanomechanical motion; applications include smart metamaterials and miniaturized light modulators.

articleTitle: Large-scale plasmonic pixels and combinatorial colors
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Film-coupled nanocubes patterned into pixels are used to demonstrate a plasmonic multispectral pixel array consisting of six resonances between 580 and 1125 nm and reconstruct an RGB image with 9261 color combinations.

articleTitle: Uncooled infrared sensor using torsional resonator and electrostatic detection
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: A new torsional resonator is designed for the infrared sensor. The actuation uses the fringe field from the vertical sidewall. The electrostatic detection bases on the transmitted voltage to the electrode near to the resonator.

articleTitle: Fabrication of plasmonic color filter by freestanding metal-insulator-metal gratings for MEMS tunable filter
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: This paper reports on a plasmonic color filter by freestanding metal-insulator-metal (MIM) subwavelength gratings. Fabricated MIM gratings were demonstrated transmissive multispectral color filters based on surface plasmons by changing the period of the grating.

articleTitle: Forward-looking OCT endomicroscope based on a compact Fourier-plane piezo fiber scanner
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We present an endoscopic OCT probe featuring a piezo-tube-actuated Fourier-plane fiber scanner, which has 2 mm field-of-view and 29 μm lateral resolution. With 3 mm outer diameter and only 11mm in length, the probe is the shortest reported probe of this type and offers a good solution for flexible endomicroscopy within confined volumes.

articleTitle: Fabrication of large-area optical antenna arrays for studying spontaneous emission enhancement of 2D transition metal dichalcogenide
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We report a wafer-scale fabrication process to make large-area slot antenna arrays for studying spontaneous emission enhancement of 2D transition metal dichalcogenide. The experimental results show a 10-fold enhancement of photoluminescence was observed.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable MEMS metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: The properties of the metamaterials strongly depend on the geometrical shape and size of the subwavelength unit cell. Active control of metamaterial provides effective ways of manipulating electromagnetic waves in THz spectral domain. Reconfigurable microcantilevers integrated into programmable unit cells in various layouts have been investigated to realize novel tunable THz metamaterials. In this paper, we review the recent progress in the MEMS based reconfigurable metamaterials.

articleTitle: Development of electrothermal lens actuator for endoscopic blood flow sensor
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: A novel blood flow sensor enabling a precise measurement in an endoscope has been developed. In this paper, a device design and a validity of an electrothermal actuator for the lens control are reported.

articleTitle: An electromagnetic two-axis micro scanner with dual radial magnetic fields
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: An electromagnetic scanner with dual radial magnetic fields was developed to enlarge torque in both horizontal and vertical scans. Scan angles were 50.55° and 9.06° for horizontal and vertical scans, respectively, for single current path.

articleTitle: Portable multispectra tunable forensic lens for jadeite analysis
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: This paper purposes a portable multispectra tunable forensic lens for jadeite analysis. The visible and ultraviolet light are used to detect the absorption spectra of natural jadeite, implement jadeite, and jadeite color spectra around 550~700 nm. Besides, tunable lens with three-step (5, 7 and 10 X) magnification is based on the dielectric liquid lens.

articleTitle: Design of tunable SPR on MEMS for displays
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: A tunable surface plasmonic resonance (SPR) driven by microelectromechanical system (MEMS) is designed in this work. Pitch tuning of SPR structures on elastomer filters various transmission of electromagnetic (EM) spectra. A color filter based on SPR in the visible range is proposed and evaluated at various strains induced by the MEMS operation before quantified by figure of merit. Distinguishable EM spectra realized with the proposed design implied a solution to single pixel (subpixel) full color display operated in a time-sequential manner.

articleTitle: Keynote We-K: Microscale light emitting diodes: From information display to discovery tools in neuroscience
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Recent advances in materials science and engineering provide means for constructing high-performance light emitting diodes with unusual sizes, shapes and forms and with efficient operation throughout the infrared, visible and ultraviolet. When combined with high-speed assembly techniques, microscale devices of this type can be configured onto ultrathin polymer filaments for injection into biological tissues, onto elastomeric substrates for use in skin-conformal health diagnostics, and into large-scale sparse arrays for high-speed displays with unmatched brightness, contrast, switching speeds and power efficiency. This talk summarizes the foundational scientific concepts and the engineering designs for these and other applications.

articleTitle: Black silicon based iris with reduced light scattering and reflection
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: This paper reports the fabrication and the characterization of a black silicon based iris that shows significant reduction in the unwanted stray light due to scattering and reflection on the iris surfaces. The iris was characterized by recording the far-field diffraction pattern at a 532-nm wavelength. The intensity at dark rings is reduced by a factor of up to 5, which makes the bright 0<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> order disk much sharper.

articleTitle: Vacuum radiometry of an infrared nanoantenna-coupled tunnel diode rectenna
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We examine the vacuum infrared photoresponse of a large-area nanoantenna-coupled tunnel diode rectenna resulting from thermal radiation from a temperature controlled heater. The measured infrared photocurrent is obtained as a function of the source temperature, sample distance and view factor. Far-field radiation power conversion is examined using standard radiometric techniques and correlated with the rectified current response.

articleTitle: Optoelectro microfluidic chip for sequential sensing of mass diffusion coefficient
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Optoelectro-microfluidic sensor based on a laser-induced dielectrophoresis is developed for the biological sensing. A sequential sensing of mass diffusion coefficient is demonstrated using two nanobeads sample.

articleTitle: Tunable room-temperature single-photon emission at telecom wavelengths from sp3 defects in carbon nanotubes
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Room temperature single photon emissions with ultra-high single photon purity and enhanced emission stability are observed at telecom band from Quantum defects of single-wall carbon nanotubes.

articleTitle: Photothermal intracellular delivery with self-aligned cell seeding
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We demonstrated a photothermal delivery approach with self-aligned cell seeding, which was realized by simple fabrication of microwells and sharp tips. Calcein molecules (622 Da) were successfully delivered into cells with above 80% viability.

articleTitle: Temperature and distance dependence of plasmon enhanced InAs/InGaAs/GaAs dot-in-a-well near IR emission
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Using gold nanorods (AuNRs) as plasmonic structures to couple the InAs QD emitter for enhancing carrier generation and photon emission, temperature dependent PL emission over a range of 10K to room temperature has been studied systematically by varying the GaAs thickness.

articleTitle: Feasibility study of the OCT probe using MEMS optical scanner array for high speed inspection
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We developed a microscanner-based optical coherence tomography probe for the 3-dimensional inspection of display panels, which will be extended to arrayed scanners to enhance inspection speed. The scanning range and beam diameter were 13.1 mm and 84.5 μm, respectively.

articleTitle: Dynamical range and stability enhancement in electrically fused microknot optical resonators
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We present a simple robust local electrical fusing approach for microknot resonators using a two-probe technique. These devices exhibit significantly improved optical performance and mechanical stability, and can be applied in next generation optomechanical sensors.

articleTitle: High-throughput fabrication of surface plasmon resonance fiber probes using nanotransfer printing method
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We demonstrate a novel fabrication method to make many optical fiber sensing probes with the end face of each optical fiber patterned with submicron scale Au hole-array pattern using novel nano-transfer printing method.

articleTitle: Keynote Tu-K: Plasmonics — A path to replace photonics by a scalable, ultrafast technology?
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Plasmonics is increasingly touted as a solution to replace traditional photonics. And indeed, a new generation of passive and active plasmonic elements is emerging. Unlike photonic devices these plasmonic elements feature a tiny footprint in combination with an almost unlimited bandwidth. Yet, plasmonic devices also suffer from high losses. The question then is where and when plasmonics really can make a difference. In this talk, we will review and comment the latest generation of plasmonic devices encompassing plasmonic electro-optical modulators, detectors, RF-receivers, couplers and waveguides and compare them against devices relying on the traditional silicon technology.

articleTitle: Deep silicon etching for X-ray diffraction devices fabrication
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We report deep reactive ion etching of silicon gratings via cryogenic and Bosch processes. An aspect ratio of > 50 is achieved for 400 nm period gratings with both processes.

articleTitle: Tunable optical response and purcell enhancement of gated plasmonic structures
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate plasmonic nanostructures that enable dynamic electrical control of the phase and/or amplitude of the plane wave reflected from the nanostructures. We also demonstrate dynamically controlled Purcell enhancement of spontaneous emission of InP quantum dots (QDs) coupled to plasmonic heterostructures.

articleTitle: Selectively controlling plasmon-driven photochemical reactions
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We studied selectively catalyzed plasmon driven photochemical reactions of paraaminothiophenol (PATP) as model molecule placed in cavity between gold film (AuF) and different ligands coated gold nanorods (AuNR) by surface enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS).

articleTitle: Femtosecond switching of infrared light using a plasmonic cadmium oxide perfect absorber
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Using a high-electron-mobility cadmium oxide perfect absorber and intraband optical pumping, we experimentally demonstrate a reflective polarizer with a polarization extinction ratio of 91 that can be switched on and off within 800 fs.

articleTitle: Tunable gold nano-disks array on flexible substrates
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Low cost nanosphere lithography is used to fabricate polycrystalline nanodisk array of gold on flexible PDMS substrates. Extinction measurements reveal tunable plasmonic resonance under the influence of substrate strain. Excellent reproducibility has been demonstrated by repeated stretch and release tests.

articleTitle: Fourier reconstruction of the force signal using a microelectromechanical oscillator in the Casimir regime
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Harmonics of the force between an engineered sample and a sphere mounted on high quality factor microelectromechanical oscillator have been measured. The sample consists of regions with deep trenches and flat regions. Both the sample and the sphere are coated with a thick layer of gold. The sample is sequentially rotated at selected frequencies yielding the Casimir interaction between the sphere and the sample, disentangled from the electrostatic contribution. The approach is promising and it should yield a Casimir measurement between 0.2 and 8 microns.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic coupling mechanisms in vertically oriented metallic plasmonic inclusions
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Structured electromagnetic materials have experienced a renaissance with the emergence of metamaterial and plasmonic research. The ability to orient metallic plasmonic inclusions vertically enables orientation-dependent coupling arrangements which cannot be achieved in conventional planar engineered materials. In this paper we discuss these coupling arrangements and their effect on the measured far field scattering response to normally incident excitation.

articleTitle: Characteristics of ultra-thin MEMS mirror device on flexibe substrate
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)

articleTitle: Improved infrared detection using nanoantennas
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We examine integration of a patterned metal nanoantenna (or metasurface) directly onto long-wave infrared detectors. These structures show significantly improved external quantum efficiency compared to their traditional counterparts. We will show simulation and experimental results.
